name: Onboard & Launch Company
description: Flagship end-to-end onboarding: build a source-of-truth brand and catalog manifest, import the complete product catalog before theme work, clone the home/shop/PDP experience through independently reviewed build stages, and finish with rendered-route and launch-readiness gates. Worker and reviewer models are deliberately cross-vendor so evidence, not one model's self-assessment, decides whether the run passes.

steps.name: Gather brand & business info
acceptance: The company's website was crawled and the legal/business name, support contact, and business hours (where publicly listed) were located and reported.

Brand identity was harvested from the SOURCE (Step 3f): the palette read out of the site's own stylesheet (`:root` custom properties / dominant hexes, not eyeballed from a screenshot), the real `@font-face` family names + weights with a license verdict on each, the logo asset, and 8-12 VERBATIM lines of source copy (headlines, a product description, the primary CTA label).

`brand.md` WAS WRITTEN via the `update_brand_voice` tool (mode `replace`) and exists on disk. This is not optional and STEP_OUTPUT is not a substitute: Mist injects brand.md as a `<brand_voice>` block into every later agent turn for this company, while STEP_OUTPUT reaches only steps that declare a dependsOn, is invisible to QA reviewers, and dies with the run. Verify: `fluid_api("/api/settings/brand_guidelines","GET")` shows a non-null `brand_md`, OR — if only the API push failed — the tool reported a successful local write and the exact API error is recorded in remaining_for_human.

brand.md is SPECIFIC TO THIS BRAND, not a filled-in template. It carries the canonical headings (Brand Overview, Mission & Values, Tone of Voice, Audience, Vocabulary & Naming, Visual Style, Do's and Don'ts, Brands & Sites We Admire, Examples, Sources) and passes the substitution test: no line would read just as true for an unrelated company. Concretely it must contain real hex values, the real font family + weights + license status, the brand's actual price band / market / currency, at least 3 verbatim quoted lines of source copy, a named do/don't list including words this brand never uses, and 3 deliberately OFF-brand example lines. Generic filler ('friendly and approachable', 'modern clean design', 'quality-focused customers') is a FAIL even though the file exists.

Structured brand fields were pushed separately via PATCH /api/settings/brand_guidelines (color, secondary_color, logo_url/icon_url/favicon_url as DAM URLs) — brand.md is the prose layer and does not replace them.

Whatever onboarding/business fields could be pre-filled via the Fluid API were submitted (HIGH + MEDIUM confidence only) using the EXACT contracts in onboarding/onboarding-prefill/references/api-endpoints.md. Field pushes are BEST-EFFORT: a field whose push still fails after retrying with the documented endpoint/payload (e.g. a support email or rename returning 400) is recorded in STEP_OUTPUT.remaining_for_human with the endpoint + error and does NOT fail this step. LOW-confidence fields were reported but not pushed.

The step's STEP_OUTPUT includes the canonical website_url the rest of the workflow will use, plus a `brand_md` object: { written, path, synced_to_api, sections_filled[], sections_left_as_prompts[], palette{}, fonts[], verbatim_quotes, source_urls[] }.

HARD-FAIL BAR (the only reasons this step may fail): the website could not be crawled at all, the active company could not be confirmed, NOT A SINGLE field could be pushed, or brand.md was not written / is boilerplate. Individual FIELD failures — however many — are remainders, not failures; a failed root step cascades and kills every downstream step, so reserve failure for total blockage. Note that a brand.md that only failed to SYNC to the API is a remainder, not a failure — the local file is what `<brand_voice>` reads.

steps.name: QA brand + business data before the build
steps.prompt:
Independently verify the data gather-context produced BEFORE the product import and theme build consume it — a wrong brand color, missing font, wrong market, or a boilerplate brand.md propagates into every theme section, every piece of generated copy, and the store config. Re-fetch from the API and check against the SOURCE site; do not trust gather-context's self-report. Exact brand_guidelines contract (allowed fields incl. logo_url; PATCH body wrapped in the brand_guidelines key; logo/icon/favicon must be DAM URLs uploaded first via dam_upload): see onboarding/onboarding-prefill/references/api-endpoints.md.

1. Brand palette + type (drives the theme): GET /api/settings/brand_guidelines. Confirm primary/secondary colors are SET (not defaults/placeholders) and match the source site's actual palette. Verify against the SOURCE STYLESHEET, not a screenshot: fetch the site's main CSS bundle and read its `:root` custom properties and `@font-face` blocks. Confirm brand fonts were IDENTIFIED with a license verdict for the theme build (brand_guidelines has NO font field — do not fail QA for a missing font on that endpoint; fonts land in theme tokens).

2. brand.md — THE ARTIFACT EVERY LATER AGENT READS. Read the `<brand_voice>` block in your own context (that IS brand.md) and cross-check with `fluid_api("/api/settings/brand_guidelines","GET")` → `brand_md`. Grade it on SPECIFICITY, not existence, using the substitution test: for each section, ask 'would this sentence be equally true for an unrelated company?'. Check concretely that it contains (a) real hex values matching the stylesheet you just read, (b) the real font family + weights + whether it is licensable, (c) this brand's actual price band, market and currency, (d) at least 3 VERBATIM quoted lines of source copy — spot-check 2 of them by re-fetching the page they came from and confirming the string is really there, (e) a do/don't list naming words this brand never uses, (f) 3 deliberately off-brand example lines. A brand.md whose Tone of Voice is 'friendly and approachable' and whose Visual Style is 'modern and clean' is a FAIL — it will produce exactly the generic copy this whole check exists to prevent. If it is thin but the source data is available, REWRITE it yourself via `update_brand_voice` (mode `replace`) and re-verify; that is a fix, not a failure.

3. Countries/markets (drive currency, locale, tax, theme): GET the company countries; confirm the intended market(s) are configured with correct currency/locale, and that brand.md's stated market/currency agrees.

4. Business info (best-effort, never flag-gated): where recoverable from the source, confirm legal/business name, support contact, and business hours (where public) landed; if a field is not present or not recoverable, mark it deferred-for-human — do NOT hard-fail QA on missing business info.

5. Loop: for any field wrong/missing and recoverable from the source, fix it (re-push) and re-verify; else record it.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { brand:{colors,fonts,source_match}, brand_md:{present, specific:true|false, sections_filled, verbatim_quotes_verified, rewritten_by_qa:true|false}, countries:[...], business:{...}|'deferred', status:'pass'|'cap-reached', remaining_for_human:[...] }.
acceptance: Brand colors + fonts were verified against the SOURCE STYLESHEET (its `:root` tokens and `@font-face` blocks), not merely 'set' and not eyeballed from a screenshot — the palette handed to the theme build matches the source. A wrong/default palette that is fixable from the source this turn should be FIXED and re-verified, not failed.

brand.md was read and graded on SPECIFICITY via the substitution test — not merely confirmed to exist. The QA reports which required specifics are present (real hexes matching the stylesheet, real font family + weights + license verdict, price band / market / currency, >=3 verbatim source quotes, a do/don't list with words this brand never uses, 3 off-brand examples) and re-verified at least 2 quoted lines against the live source page.

If brand.md was missing, boilerplate, or contradicted the source, QA REWROTE it via update_brand_voice (mode `replace`) and re-verified. Reporting it as a remainder without fixing it does not satisfy this step — every downstream agent reads this file.
The intended market country/countries are configured with correct currency/locale, and brand.md's stated market/currency agrees with them.

Brand + countries correctness is confirmed, and business fields (legal/business name, support contact, business hours) were verified where recoverable from the source OR explicitly marked deferred-for-human — missing business info is a remainder, never a hard blocker.
STEP_OUTPUT reports status 'pass' or 'cap-reached' with an itemized remaining_for_human list and the brand_md verdict — no silent pass.

HARD-FAIL BAR: grading is against OUTCOMES AVAILABLE DOWNSTREAM, not push mechanics. A value that failed to persist via settings but is correctly RECORDED in STEP_OUTPUT for downstream steps (e.g. brand color the theme build applies directly) plus listed in remaining_for_human is acceptable — do not fail the run over a field-level 400. A brand.md that is present and specific LOCALLY but failed to sync to the API is a PASS with a remainder — the local file is what `<brand_voice>` injects. FAIL only when the brand palette is wrong/unverified against the source AND unrecoverable this turn, the intended market cannot be determined, or brand.md is still absent/boilerplate after QA's own rewrite attempt.

steps.name: Build and reconcile the complete source catalog manifest
steps.prompt:
Build the complete product SOURCE MANIFEST before any product write. Call run_skill("fluid-product-admin-import") and follow its Catalog completion contract. This step is read-only against Fluid.

Discovery is a union: (1) parse sitemap.xml plus every child sitemap and retain every product URL, lastmod, and sitemap image; (2) exhaust any structured catalog API until its documented empty-page/cursor terminator; (3) exhaust every collection/category pagination and collect product links; (4) fetch every unique PDP, including an advertised `.md` twin, rendered HTML/JSON-LD, and structured data as needed. A fixed batch cap such as 100 is transport chunking, never a completion limit.

For each discovered URL record immutable source_id/url/handle, requested and final URL, HTTP status/content type, title, exact price/currency, source image URLs, exact option axes and variant count, description, and evidence method. A 200 that redirects to the homepage is stale, not a live product. Markdown is copy/data evidence only: fill missing images/options from sitemap images, JSON-LD, rendered HTML, or APIs. Never exclude a product because one parser failed.

Write source-catalog.json to a fresh run-specific working directory and checkpoint every successfully resolved product. Reconcile all discovery sets. Every discovered URL must be either a live product or an explicit exclusion with objective evidence. Report duplicate-title groups because later idempotency must use immutable source identity, never title-only fallback. Compute a SHA-256 of the final manifest.

Use at most 10 concurrent source fetches, bounded retries with exponential backoff/jitter, and resume from checkpoints after interruption. End with STEP_OUTPUT: { manifest_path, manifest_sha256, observed_at, discovery:{sitemap,api,collections,unique}, live_count, excluded_count, exclusions_by_reason, unresolved_count, duplicate_title_groups, missing_fields:{title,price,images,variants}, completion_proof }.
acceptance: source-catalog.json exists and its SHA-256, observation time, and path are reported.
Discovery used the union of sitemap(s), structured catalog endpoints when available, and collection/category links; every source pagination/batch exit condition is recorded.

Every unique discovered product URL is accounted for as one live product or an evidence-backed exclusion. Redirect-to-home, parser failures, bot blocks, missing images, and batch caps are not silently counted as complete products or used as permission to stop.

Every live record has an immutable source identity plus source/final URL, status, title, exact price/currency, images, option axes, variant count, and extraction evidence; missing fields are zero or itemized as unresolved.
Duplicate-title groups are reported, and the manifest does not deduplicate distinct source handles by title.
HARD-FAIL BAR: fail when unresolved_count is nonzero, discovery was capped before exhaustion, the manifest does not reconcile every discovered URL, or the file/evidence is missing.

steps.name: Import products (Connect / scrape / manual)
steps.prompt:
Import the company's product catalog into Fluid so it MATCHES THE SOURCE — not so that rows exist. This step runs BEFORE the theme build on purpose: the theme's product and collection templates render REAL products, so the catalog must exist first. The manager step context includes a `products_source` field set by the fronting `onboarding/onboard-launch-company` skill — branch on it.

**STEP 0 (all cases except C) — BUILD THE SOURCE MANIFEST FIRST.** You cannot verify against the source without writing the source down. Before creating anything, enumerate the source catalog to a file (e.g. `/tmp/source-catalog.json`), one record per product: `{ handle/url, title, price, currency, image_urls[], option_axes:{name:[values]}, variant_count, description }`.
  - Shopify-backed source: try `<site>/products.json?limit=250&page=N` until empty — the fastest source of truth WHEN it is reachable. Some modern Shopify/Hydrogen storefronts sit behind Cloudflare and return 403 'Verifying your connection' to it. Two good fallbacks, in order: (1) some storefronts publish an LLM-oriented markdown twin at `<product-url>.md` returning clean `# Title / ![](image) / **Price**: 115 EUR / ## Description` — check for the 'A Markdown version of this page is available' banner on any page; (2) crawl every collection page — a Shopify collection card carries title + price + primary image — then hit the individual PDPs for option axes.
  - Non-Shopify: sitemap.xml + the shop/collection pages via the crawl tool; then each PDP for options, gallery images and description.
  - FILTER OUT app-helper junk before counting or importing: $0 products, subscription-upsell/cashback helpers (Aftersell 'Upgrade to Quarterly', Fondue 'CashBack', ymal/crosssell, test products). Record the filtered list and the filtered COUNT — that number, not the raw count, is what you reconcile against.
  - Report `source_count` from this manifest. A run with no source manifest cannot claim a match rate and will not pass QA.

**Case A — `products_source: "connect"`**
  A Connect droplet (Shopify / Exigo / ByDesign / Pillars / Infotrax) was chosen. The context also has `connect_provider` (slug) and `connect_droplet_uuid`.
  1. GET /api/droplets/{connect_droplet_uuid} and confirm `is_connected: true`. If not, drop through to Case B and note the switch in your report.
  2. Trigger the droplet's product-sync entrypoint. Providers today expose different sync verbs (Shopify: `POST /api/droplets/{uuid}/sync?resource=products`; others: check the droplet's own actions). If unsure, GET /api/droplets/{uuid} and read `settings.actions` for the sync endpoint.
  3. Poll GET /api/company/v1/products until the count stops climbing (or 60 s elapses), then report the final count from `meta.pagination.total_count`.
  4. A sync is NOT self-certifying. Run the same Step 4 reconciliation below against the source manifest — Connect syncs routinely drop images, options or descriptions.

**Case B — `products_source: "scrape"`**
  1. Create each product with the NESTED-ATTRIBUTES payload (a flat `{product:{title,price}}` shape silently creates $0 shells — pricing lives on variant_countries). VERIFIED-WORKING SHAPE (live-tested 2026-07-25; the three marked keys are the ones that silently or noisily break an import):
     POST /api/company/v1/products with `{ "product": { "title", "description", "active": true, "status": "active", "images_attributes": [ { "image_url": "<DAM url>", "position": 1 } ], "option_attrs": [names...], "variants_attributes": [ { "is_master": true, "option_attrs": [values...], "variant_countries_attributes": [ { "country_id": <int>, "active": true, "currency_code": "EUR", "price": <n>, "compare_price": <n|null> } ] }, ... ] } }`.
     - `images_attributes` entries use **`image_url`**, not `url`. `{"url": …}` 422s with `image_url is missing`.
     - `variant_countries_attributes` entries require **`country_id` (integer) and `active`**. `country_iso` alone 422s with `active is missing, country_id is missing`. Get the integer from `GET /api/settings/company_countries` → `company_countries[].country.id`; never hard-code an example country ID. This one is the classic cause of a catalog that ends up with correct titles and no pricing.
     - Exactly one variant has `is_master: true`. Product-level `option_attrs` are option NAMES, variant-level are VALUES (lengths must match; a lone 'Default Title' variant gets none).
     - Set options + all variants **at CREATE time**. Adding an option axis to an already-created single-variant product via PATCH returns a 422 with an EMPTY errors object — there is no supported repair path, so a product imported flat has to be re-created to gain its variants. Get it right on the first POST.
  2. **CARRY THE VARIANTS ACROSS.** If the source PDP offers colours, sizes, or any other axis, the Fluid product must have the SAME option names and the SAME values, one variant per real combination. Collapsing a multi-variant product into a single master variant is a silent data-loss bug: the storefront loses its selector, add-to-cart binds to one arbitrary id, and the add-to-cart QA step later reports every PDP as 'not variant-aware'. A catalog where every product has exactly one variant, when the source has colourways or sizes, does NOT satisfy this step.
  3. **CARRY THE IMAGES ACROSS.** Use the `dam_upload` tool, or POST multipart to https://upload.fluid.app/upload with the actual file bytes (fields in this order: `fileName`, `file`, then `name`/`tags`) after downloading the source image. There is **no `external_asset_url` on this endpoint** — a JSON body 400s with `Either b64_json or data_uri is required`. Take `asset.default_variant_url` from the response and put it in `images_attributes[].image_url`. Never hotlink source CDNs. A product left on Fluid's grey placeholder (`image_url` ending `/placeholders/image.jpg`, `images: []`) is an unfinished import, not a stylistic choice — the source listing card already gave you a real image URL for every product.
  4. Use the source's own DESCRIPTION and the source's own PRICE + currency. Do not paraphrase, do not round, do not invent marketing copy — and read `brand.md` (the `<brand_voice>` block in your context) before writing any copy you do have to author.
  5. Do NOT attach subscription plans the source does not offer. Bulk-attaching a 'Monthly' plan at the full retail amount can make a one-time product render at that same amount per month on the PDP.
  6. NOTE: Fluid re-slugifies from the title and may append a uuid to every slug — match existing products by SLUG with TITLE fallback, and use each created product's canonical_url/slug from the API (not the source handle) when linking. Idempotency: GET /api/company/v1/products first and skip products that already exist.

**Case C — `products_source: "manual"`**
  1. Create exactly one stub product with title 'Sample Product', description 'Replace me before launch.', price 0. This unblocks onboarding without pretending the catalog is real.
  2. Explicitly report 'MANUAL ENTRY REQUIRED for N products' and list what was found on the site (from a light crawl) so the human has a checklist.

**STEP 4 (Cases A + B) — RECONCILE AGAINST THE SOURCE, THEN FIX WHAT DRIFTED.** Grading yourself on 'products exist' is the bug this step is trying not to repeat.
  a. **Coverage** — compare `meta.pagination.total_count` (never the returned array length; pagination caps it) with `source_count` from your manifest. Report both and the percentage.
  b. **Field-level sample** — take a RANDOM sample of at least 10 imported products (or all of them if fewer), and ALWAYS include the source's most expensive/flagship product and one multi-variant product. For each, compare against its source manifest record: title matches; price + currency match exactly; image count >= 1 and the images resolve on the Fluid DAM (not a placeholder, not a source CDN URL); option axes and variant count match; description is the source's, not invented.
  c. **Fix, then re-verify.** Every mismatch you can repair from the manifest (missing images, missing variants, wrong price) gets repaired this step and re-checked. Do not hand a fixable mismatch to the QA steps downstream.
  d. Report a per-field match rate, not a vibe.

Always end with STEP_OUTPUT: `{ products_source, source_count, imported_count, coverage_pct, sample:[{title, source_price, fluid_price, images, source_images, variants, source_variants, match}], match_rates:{title,price,images,variants,description}, missing_from_fluid:[titles], junk_filtered:[titles], failures:[], remaining_for_human:[] }` — and for Case C, the list of products the human still has to add.
acceptance: A SOURCE MANIFEST was built before importing (Cases A/B): the source catalog was enumerated to a concrete list of {source_url, title, price, currency, images, option axes, variant count} with app-helper/$0 junk filtered out, `source_count` is reported from it, and the enumeration method + exit condition are recorded (all sitemap/collection pages exhausted, API pagination returned empty, or equivalent). 'Products exist in Fluid' proves nothing without a demonstrably complete source number.

The importer consumed the exact source-catalog.json path + SHA-256 produced by catalog-source-manifest; it did not replace the reviewed denominator with a smaller collection-page list or a new ad-hoc crawl.

COVERAGE: the imported catalog is 100% of the filtered source manifest and `missing_from_fluid` is empty. A source item may be excluded only when it is recorded in `junk_filtered` with objective evidence that it is not a sellable catalog product. Bot blocks, API errors, and partial pagination are recovery work, not permission to call a partial catalog complete.

IDENTITY: every live source_id maps to one distinct Fluid product ID in a persisted checkpoint, no two source identities map to the same Fluid ID, and duplicate source titles were not collapsed by title-only fallback. Each successful create was checkpointed before the next item so restart/resume is idempotent.

TITLES + PRICES match the source: on a random sample of >=10 imported products (or all, if fewer) that INCLUDES the flagship/most-expensive product and one multi-variant product, each title matches its source record and the price + currency match the source exactly on the default country's `variant_countries` pricing. Non-zero is not the bar — CORRECT is the bar.

IMAGES match the source: sampled products each have >=1 real image hosted on the Fluid DAM. A product on Fluid's grey placeholder (`images: []` / `image_url` ending `/placeholders/image.jpg`) or hotlinking the source CDN counts as NOT imported for that product. Report the count of placeholder-only products across the WHOLE catalog, not just the sample — it must be 0, or every exception named with a reason.

VARIANTS match the source: where the source PDP offers colours / sizes / any option axis, the Fluid product has the same option names and values and one variant per real combination. A whole catalog sitting at exactly one master variant per product, when the source has colourways or sizes, is silent data loss and fails this criterion — it also guarantees the later add-to-cart QA finds every PDP non-variant-aware.

Imported products are `status: "active"`, descriptions come from the source (not invented marketing copy), no duplicate slugs were created, and $0 app-helper junk was excluded rather than imported. No subscription plan was attached that the source does not offer(a full-retail 'Monthly' plan bulk-attached to every product can falsely render one-time retail prices as monthly charges and fails this criterion).

Mismatches that were repairable from the manifest (missing images, collapsed variants, wrong price) were FIXED and re-verified during this step, not deferred to the QA steps. STEP_OUTPUT reports source_count, imported_count, coverage_pct, the per-product sample table, and per-field match_rates — spot-checkable numbers, not a self-assessment.
For Case C: the report explicitly says 'MANUAL ENTRY REQUIRED' and names how many products need human entry; the stub is the only product created.

HARD-FAIL BAR: for Cases A/B, fail when the source manifest is missing/incomplete, coverage is below 100%, a sellable source product is missing, or the sample shows systemic drift — $0/placeholder-priced shells, placeholder images across the catalog, collapsed source variants, or draft products. Case C remains an explicit manual-entry outcome and must never be presented as a completed catalog.

steps.name: Theme 1/6 — scrape source + section inventory + DAM assets
steps.prompt:
First theme step. You are in a scaffolded Fluid base-theme project. Call run_skill("themes/theme-clone") and execute its discovery phases only: page discovery, content scraping, rendered visual audit, source CSS/token extraction, and DAM asset upload. Do not build sections or templates yet.

Build three evidence layers instead of treating one crawl payload as truth:
1. CONTENT/DATA — use AI-friendly Markdown when advertised plus sitemap/collection/PDP content for exact copy and catalog facts. Markdown is not visual truth.
2. DOM/TOKENS — retain rendered HTML with global chrome (`only_main_content:false`) and inspect linked stylesheets, CSS custom properties, @font-face declarations, and layout geometry.
3. VISUAL — follow themes/theme-clone/references/dev-preview-visual-diff.md. In Mist, use managed `crawl` with `screenshot_options:{full_page:true,quality:90,viewport:{width,height}}`; capture home, shop, and PDP at 1440x900 and 390x844. This must work without local/global Playwright. Inspect HTML before using a constrained click action to dismiss a geo/cookie/newsletter overlay, then record the selector/action. A redirected, blank, loading, or obscured screenshot is invalid.

Priority routes are the homepage, the source's primary shop/collection index, and the flagship or most complex multi-variant PDP. Inventory EVERY visible section on all three in source order, plus global header/footer. Inspect up to two more PDPs and four key static pages for content/structure coverage. Download and dam_upload every asset required by the priority routes; record asset.default_variant_url. Extract real font families/weights and a license/substitution decision. The source wins any disagreement with gather-context, but record the conflict.

Write `clone-manifest.json` at the theme root with: source_url, page_manifest, section_inventory for home/shop/PDP/header/footer, brand_tokens, dam_assets, and `visual_routes` entries for home/shop/pdp. Each visual route contains source_url, future built_path, ordered landmarks `{id,source_selector,built_selector}` for every visible priority section, and current desktop/mobile source evidence paths plus final URL/status/overlay handling. Built selectors use stable template section ids chosen now so later build steps implement the manifest rather than inventing mappings afterward.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: manifest path, priority route URLs, per-route landmark counts, 6/6 clean source baseline paths, page count, uploaded asset count, brand tokens, and non-priority gaps.
acceptance: `clone-manifest.json` exists at the theme project root and contains a page manifest, home + shop + representative-PDP section inventories with concrete computed style values, header/footer inventory, brand tokens (colors + fonts with licensing notes), and a source-URL → DAM-URL asset map — verify by READING the file, not the worker's claim.

The manifest has `visual_routes.home`, `visual_routes.shop`, and `visual_routes.pdp`. Each records source_url, built_path, and an ordered landmark list mapping every visible priority source section selector to a stable built section id/selector.

Source discovery used three distinct evidence layers: AI-friendly Markdown for copy/catalog facts, rendered HTML/CSS for DOM/tokens/fonts, and clean managed-browser full-page screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 for visual structure. The source matrix is 6/6 (home/shop/PDP × desktop/mobile), each baseline records final URL + HTTP status + overlay handling, and none is obscured, redirected, blank, or stale.
Spot-check 2-3 DAM URLs from the manifest: they resolve to real images (HTTP 200).
The section inventory covers every visible home, shop, and representative-PDP section in source order (compare against the live rendered pages).

HARD-FAIL BAR: fail when any priority route could not be captured cleanly, a priority landmark inventory is incomplete, the manifest is missing/empty, or zero required images landed on the DAM. Non-priority static-page gaps can remain itemized notes.

steps.name: Theme 2/6 — design tokens + skeleton boots
steps.prompt:
Wire the source site's design tokens into the theme so every later section references them. Call run_skill("themes/theme-clone") and execute ONLY Phase 4b (Theme Config Setup) using `clone-manifest.json`'s brand_tokens:

1. `config/settings_data.json`: set the 12-color palette + 5-font palette + heading sizes from the manifest (every font slot seeded — defaults in settings_schema.json do NOT auto-apply to missing keys).
2. `config/settings_schema.json`: confirm every color/font setting carries its `option_group` (background_colors / font_families) — sections' dropdowns are empty without them.
3. `layouts/theme.liquid`: all 12 `--clr-*` and 5 `--ff-*` CSS variables wired in :root with `| default:` fallbacks. If the source font is importable, add the @font-face (note the licensing disclaimer in a comment); otherwise use the manifest's chosen substitute and note it.
4. Honor the caller context's `theme_target`: `new` → this scaffolded project is the target; `existing` with `theme_id` → record that id as the push target for later steps. Record the decision in clone-manifest.json under `theme_target_resolved`.
5. Call `start_preview` to boot the long-lived dev server with Mist's bundled CLI and port manager; never run a dev server through bounded `run_cli`. Call `preview_state`, `read_local_server_logs`, `read_preview_console`, and `screenshot_preview` to confirm the skeleton renders (base-theme placeholder content is fine at this point).

End with STEP_OUTPUT: tokens set (colors/fonts), font licensing decision, theme_target_resolved, local URL/port, and preview/log status.
acceptance: settings_data.json + settings_schema.json parse as valid JSON; the 12 color slots and 5 font slots are populated with the manifest's brand values (not base-theme defaults), and every color/font setting has its option_group.
layouts/theme.liquid wires all --clr-* and --ff-* variables with | default: fallbacks; the font decision (real @font-face or named substitute) is recorded.
The dev preview boots and renders without server errors — verified with a screenshot_preview this turn (placeholder content is acceptable; this step is about tokens + skeleton, not content).

HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only when a config file is invalid/unwritten, tokens still hold base-theme defaults, or the dev preview cannot boot. Imperfect color mapping or a debatable font substitute is a NOTE for the refine pass.

steps.name: Theme 3/6 — header, navigation & footer
steps.prompt:
Build the global chrome: `sections/main_navbar` and `sections/main_footer` matched to the source site's header/footer using clone-manifest.json (inventory + DAM assets). Call run_skill("themes/theme-clone") for the section architecture rules (Section Shell + Container, blocks for content, tokens not hex, canonical blocks/components).

Requirements:
- Navbar: source's logo (DAM URL), nav items mirroring the source's top-level navigation but pointing at FLUID routes (/home, /home/collections/<slug>, /home/pages/<slug> …); working mobile hamburger; PRESERVE Fluid's JS hooks verbatim (#show-cart, #fluid-cart-count, #show-language-country-dropdown, .saveLocaleBtn, .country-selector, .language-selector — the canonical navbar components own these; render them, never rewrite).

steps.name: Theme 4/6 — homepage sections
steps.prompt:

Using clone-manifest.json's homepage section inventory, compose `home_page/default/index.liquid` from the base theme's canonical section library (heroes, image_text_split, feature_grid, featured_products, testimonial_grid, faq_accordion, cta_banner_v2 …) — call run_skill("themes/theme-clone") for the library list and section rules. steps.name: Theme 5/6 — product & collection templates
steps.prompt:

If the run has no products (products out of scope or manual stub), verify the templates render the placeholder/empty state cleanly and note it.
- Audit gate: `python3 scripts/theme_audit.py` on all touched files.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: templates written, which real product/collection routes were verified with screenshots, audit result, refine notes.
acceptance: product/default/index.liquid leads with the scaffold's canonical product-data section (product_hero or main_product — unmodified, not a hand-rolled replacement) and adds source-matching sections after it; collection/default exists and renders.

At least one REAL product PDP and one collection route were loaded in the dev preview this turn without server/Liquid errors, with screenshots (or, when the catalog is legitimately empty for this run scope, the empty state renders cleanly and is noted).
`python3 scripts/theme_audit.py` passes on the touched files.

steps.name: Theme 6/6 — content pages, full audit & push
steps.prompt:
Finish and ship the theme. Call run_skill("themes/theme-clone") for Phases 5-7.

1. Content page templates: from clone-manifest.json's page manifest (max 4 key static pages — about/faq/contact/policies), build `page/<slug>/index.liquid` templates with the scraped copy + DAM images. (Page RESOURCE records are created later by the content-import step — templates only here.)
2. Audit gate: `python3 scripts/theme_audit.py` on every file this clone TOUCHED (new or modified — check `git status`/your step notes) — fix every violation there. Then run it across the whole theme for visibility: the stock base-theme scaffold currently ships with ~100+ pre-existing violations in canonical sections you never touched; do NOT try to fix those (that's upstream base-theme work) — count them and record the per-rule rollup as a note in remaining_for_refine.
3. Push: `fluid theme push` from the theme dir. API fallback gotchas (from live runs): a fresh company ships a provisioned active 'Base' theme; POST /api/application_themes with status:"active" 500s (RecordNotUnique) while another active theme exists — create WITHOUT status, upload resources, then PATCH {application_theme:{status:"active"}} to activate (honoring `theme_target_resolved` from clone-manifest.json — `existing` pushes to that theme_id). If the CLI push fails, fall back to the resource API per the skill.
4. Verify after push: dev preview still healthy (screenshot_preview), and GET /api/application_themes confirms the landing theme exists; record its id. Then verify EVERY route type on the LIVE storefront in a real browser: home, one collection, one real product PDP (follow a link the storefront renders — do NOT trust the API's canonical_url, its slug goes stale after title PATCHes), and each content page. STALE-TEMPLATE GOTCHA (hit on every live run): a route whose MAIN region renders empty, or that falls through to the home template, has a stale application_theme_template record — resource PUTs around theme creation do not reliably re-expand them. Fix deterministically: find the record in GET /api/application_themes/{id} (match themeable_type + name), DELETE /api/application_theme_templates/{tpl_id}, re-PUT the matching template resource, wait ~10s, re-check. Applies to home_page, product, collection, and page templates alike.
5. Aggregate every 'refine note' recorded by theme steps 1-5 plus your own into a single `remaining_for_refine` list.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: theme id, pages/templates shipped, audit summary (0 violations), push result, and the aggregated remaining_for_refine list the refine step will consume.
acceptance: `python3 scripts/theme_audit.py` exits 0 on every file the clone touched (new/modified templates, sections, configs). Pre-existing violations in UNTOUCHED base-theme scaffold files are recorded as a note with the per-rule rollup — they are not this step's failure.
The theme was pushed: GET /api/application_themes shows the landing theme and STEP_OUTPUT records its id (verify via the API, not the worker's claim).

Every route type (home, collection, one real PDP followed from a storefront-rendered link, each content page) renders its own template's content in a real browser after the push — no empty main regions, no home-template fallbacks (stale application_theme_template records were refreshed via DELETE + re-PUT where needed).
Key static page TEMPLATES from the manifest exist (up to 4); STEP_OUTPUT carries the aggregated remaining_for_refine list.

Authored copy obeys `brand.md`. Mist injects the company's brand guide into every turn as a `<brand_voice>` block; scraped source strings win, and any string the agent had to write itself is in that voice and consistent with its Do's and Don'ts. Surviving base-theme placeholder copy — "NEW DROP", "Built different", "Trusted by thousands", "Shop the drop", lorem — is a defect even when the layout matches, and is the single most visible way a clone reads as generic.

HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only when the push did not land (no theme id verifiable via the API), audit violations remain, or the preview is broken after push. A shorter-than-hoped page list or a long remaining_for_refine list is fine — the refine pass exists for that.

steps.name: Iterative screenshot-based theme refine
acceptance: Phase A CODE-parity gate ran FIRST and reported CODE_PARITY: pass before any screenshot round: per-template structural comparison vs the source (sections present + ordered), brand tokens (no hardcoded hex/fonts), lint clean (no Liquid errors in the dev server log), every template route renders, and COPY/VOICE parity against `brand.md` (the `<brand_voice>` block) with no surviving base-theme placeholder copy. Screenshots are the granular FINAL pass — a run that started pixel-diffing before code parity does not satisfy this step.

The skill ran up to five semantic source-vs-clone rounds over home, shop, and PDP at desktop and mobile, and reported STATUS: pass. `cap-reached` is an honest needs-review outcome, not acceptance for the flagship workflow.

The final same-round evidence shows zero majors on all three priority routes, at most two itemized minors per route, no missing/reordered landmarks, correct copy/data/primary imagery, and priority landmark geometry within 5% unless responsive reflow is explicitly demonstrated.
STEP_OUTPUT names every route and viewport verified and includes current screenshot + metrics paths generated after the final code change.
The theme's dev preview is still healthy, every touched file passes theme_audit.py, and the final desktop/mobile routes have no Liquid errors or horizontal document overflow.
HARD-FAIL BAR: fail when the loop never ran, the preview is broken, evidence is stale/fabricated, any priority route retains a major, or the run ends `cap-reached`.

steps.name: Import every page as a resource (collections, categories, pages, posts, menus)
steps.prompt:
Create EVERY page on the source site as its Fluid RESOURCE — not just products (products are handled by products-import), and not just templates (the theme steps copied the layouts). Two axes must both be satisfied: (1) each page/URL on the source becomes a Fluid resource record, and (2) each page-type template was shipped by the theme track. This step owns axis (1) for non-product content. Follow the `fluid-product-admin-import` skill for the exact payloads.

FIRST: if context flag `import_products` is not true, emit STEP_OUTPUT { skipped: true, reason: 'content out of scope' } and return.

Enumerate the full source site (sitemap.xml + crawl — or reuse the theme track's clone-manifest.json page manifest when present) and, for each URL, create the matching resource — idempotent (GET-before-POST, skip existing, no duplicates):
- **Collections** → POST /api/company/v1/collections (with product membership). Exclude $0 app-helper/internal collections (subscription tiers, ymal/crosssell, test) — see the skill's junk-filter note.
- **Categories** → POST /api/company/v1/categories, ONLY if the source has a curated category taxonomy distinct from collections (else skip, correct-by-design).
- **Static pages** (/pages/*: about, faq, contact, shipping, policies, etc.) → create a page resource for each. Use the pages endpoint per the skill (note: POST /api/company/pages currently works; the /v1/pages variant may 404 pending a fix — do not build a client-side fallback). The theme was already pushed by the theme track — that is why this step depends on it (page creation auto-generates theme templates a later theme push would delete).
- **Blog posts** (/blogs/*/*) → POST /api/posts for each published article (title, body, hero image via DAM, date, slug). If the source blog has 0 published articles, that's correctly 0.
- **Menus / nav** → POST /api/menus to mirror the source header/footer navigation so links resolve.

Space out page-create bursts (WAF throttles them). After creating, RE-COUNT each type via its list endpoint (meta.pagination.total_count) and reconcile against the source. End with STEP_OUTPUT: { collections:{source,created}, categories:{...}, pages:{source,created}, posts:{...}, menus:{...}, skipped_junk:[...], remaining_for_human:[...] }.
acceptance: If import_products was not selected, the step correctly skipped and did no work.

Otherwise: every source collection (minus $0 app/internal junk), every curated category (or justified none), every static /pages/* page, every published blog post, and the site nav/menus were created as Fluid resources — reconciled against the source via each type's list-endpoint total_count (report exact source-vs-created counts per type).
Creates are idempotent (GET-before-POST, no duplicates on re-run); legitimately-empty types (e.g. no blog articles) are justified, not fabricated.
STEP_OUTPUT reports per-type source-vs-created counts and any remaining_for_human items.

HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only when a whole resource TYPE that clearly exists on the source was never attempted, duplicates were created, or counts were fabricated. Per-item failures (a page create 403'd by the WAF, one post failed) recorded in remaining_for_human are notes, not failures.

steps.name: Reconcile onboarding info
steps.prompt:
Reconcile the company's server-side onboarding record with what this run actually produced. NOTE: the legacy checklist endpoints (`/api/v1/onboardings`, `check_step`, `complete_step`) are REMOVED from api.fluid.app — they 404. Do NOT chase them. The live surface is:

1. Resolve the active company id (GET /api/me → company.id, or /api/settings/companies).
2. GET /api/companies/{id}/onboarding_info — read what's on file (country_code, countries_info, entity, settlement currency, business fields).
3. Cross-check against the gather-context step's output: for any field the run gathered with HIGH confidence that is empty on the record (e.g. country/entity basics), PATCH /api/companies/{id}/onboarding_info with just that field. Never overwrite non-empty values; never push LOW-confidence data. KYC/payments fields that require human/legal input are ALWAYS deferred, never fabricated.
4. Report: fields already set, fields this step filled, fields deferred to the human with reasons ('requires payments KYC', 'requires legal entity docs', 'human decision').

This step is best-effort reporting — an honest 'endpoint returned <status>, nothing writable' report with the exact request/response is a VALID outcome. End with STEP_OUTPUT: { onboarding_info_read: true|false, fields_set:[...], fields_filled:[...], deferred:[{field,reason}], endpoint_notes:[...] }.
acceptance: The step made a real GET /api/companies/{id}/onboarding_info call this turn (or documented its exact failure status) — the report cites concrete fields from the actual response, and does NOT call the removed /api/v1/onboardings endpoints.
No non-empty server value was overwritten; nothing LOW-confidence or KYC-sensitive was pushed; every deferred field has an explicit reason.
STEP_OUTPUT follows the documented shape with fields_set / fields_filled / deferred.

HARD-FAIL BAR: fail only for fabrication (claiming reads/writes the API doesn't show) or destructive overwrites. 'Read-only outcome, everything deferred to the human' is a PASSING outcome when reported honestly.

steps.name: Discover TikTok / UGC content for the DAM
steps.prompt:
FIRST: if context flag `discover_ugc` is not true, emit STEP_OUTPUT { skipped:true, reason:'discover_ugc not selected' } and return. NOTE: this is OTHER PEOPLE's content about the brand (UGC); the brand's OWN channel content is the separate brand-social-import step. Otherwise proceed.

Find user-generated and social content for this company and load it into the Fluid DAM. This step is best-effort — a company with no discoverable social presence is a valid outcome.

1. From the gather-context step's output, pull TikTok / Instagram handles. If none were found there, run one social_search (platform tiktok) with the company name as a keyword to double-check.
2. If no handles and no keyword hits: emit a short 'no discoverable UGC presence — queries attempted: [...]' report and return. This is acceptance, not failure.
3. Otherwise, for 3-8 promising videos, use the video_ripper tool to download and dam_upload to push into the company's DAM. Tag uploads with the brand name from gather-context.
4. Report every DAM asset URL you created.
acceptance: Either at least one UGC asset was uploaded to the DAM (verifiable via its reported URL), or an explicit finding documents no discoverable social/UGC presence with the queries tried.
No unrelated or off-brand content was uploaded.

steps.name: Import the brand's own YouTube + TikTok content
steps.prompt:
FIRST: if context flag `import_brand_social` is not true, emit STEP_OUTPUT { skipped:true, reason:'import_brand_social not selected' } and return (passes QA as a correct skip). Otherwise follow the `marketing/brand-social-import` skill exactly.

Imports the COMPANY'S OWN social video content — NOT UGC. (1) Resolve the company's official YouTube + TikTok accounts from gather-context social links / the site footer (confirm via social_search platform:tiktok user-mode only if unlinked — never import an unconfirmed account); (2) register confirmed handles via PATCH /api/settings/social_media (GET first, don't clobber); (3) enumerate each account's videos (TikTok: social_search platform:tiktok mode:user; YouTube: social_search platform:youtube mode:user with the handle or UC… channel id); (4) rip each via video_ripper (DAM + Media in one call) tagged `brand-content,<platform>,<brand>` — idempotent, skip already-imported, never abort on one failure. Report accounts registered, videos found/ripped/skipped/failed with DAM URLs.
acceptance: If import_brand_social was not selected, the step correctly skipped (STEP_OUTPUT skipped:true) and did no work.
Otherwise: official accounts were resolved (site links, or search-confirmed — no unconfirmed accounts) and registered via PATCH /api/settings/social_media.

Otherwise: each account's videos were ripped into DAM + Media tagged `brand-content` (never `ugc`), idempotently, per-video failures noted without aborting; or an explicit finding documents no discoverable official social presence.
No UGC / other-people's content was imported by this step (that is ugc-discovery).

steps.name: Verify links resolve to the right resource templates
steps.prompt: Audit EVERY link in the storefront and make each point to a valid, correctly-rendering Fluid resource template — this is the step that catches nav items wired to dead or generic routes. Cover: the header navigation, the footer (support / legal / social / localization), and primary in-page CTAs (hero, category tiles, banners). For each link, resolve the target and confirm it (a) returns HTTP 200 and (b) renders the CORRECT template: collection links -> collection template, category -> category, page -> page, product -> /home/products/<slug>, home -> home. FIX links that point to: a dead or generic route (e.g. a bare `/shop` that 204s instead of `/home/shop`), the wrong template, a Shopify-style URL that doesn't map to Fluid's `/home/...` routes, or a 302/404/406. EVERY resource-DETAIL href the theme emits MUST carry the credit segment (`/home/products/<slug>`, `/home/collections/<slug>`, `/home/pages/<slug>`, `/home/posts/<slug>`) — a bare `/products/<slug>` 404s at the origin and only appears to work once the CDN has cached the `/home/...` render, then breaks again when that cache entry ages out. Test each link COLD: if a bare detail URL returns 200, re-test it against a slug you have not visited this run before believing it. Also grep the rendered HTML for the unsubstituted credit placeholder `__fluid_affiliate_username__` — it resolves by fallback but must be replaced with `home` (or a real Liquid credit variable) in the theme source. Navigation menu items MUST map to real resources — e.g. 'By Scent' -> a collections/scent index (`/home/collections`), NOT a generic shop URL; 'Best Sellers' -> `/home/collections/best-sellers`; 'Gifts & Sets' -> `/home/collections/sets`. Prefer binding the nav to a real Fluid navigation menu (link_list) with correct resource URLs so it stays admin-manageable; otherwise correct the hrefs. Point footer info links at the imported pages (`/home/pages/<slug>`). A PDP (or any resource type) that returns 204/blank or 500 on its CREDIT-PREFIXED URL is NOT 'platform-side' — it almost always means the active theme has no `default: true` template for that themeable_type (check `GET /api/application_themes/active` -> application_theme_templates grouped by themeable_type). Fix the theme; do not wave it through. SLUG GOTCHA: enumerate PDP URLs from links the STOREFRONT renders (collection/search pages), not from the API's canonical_url — a PATCH that includes the title re-slugifies the product (new uuid suffix) and the old canonical_url silently falls through to the home template. End with STEP_OUTPUT containing a table: link label -> target URL -> HTTP status -> resolved template.
acceptance: Every header-nav, footer, and primary in-page link resolves to HTTP 200 and the correct resource template, asserted on the credit-prefixed URL. A PDP/collection/page that 204s or 500s is treated as a theme template-default gap to fix, not a platform excuse.
No link points to a dead/generic route (e.g. a bare `/shop`), a Shopify-style URL, or the wrong template type.
No emitted resource-detail href is bare (`/products/<slug>`) or contains `__fluid_affiliate_username__`; every one carries the `/home/` credit segment.

Navigation menu items map to real resources (By Scent -> a collections/scent index, Best Sellers -> the best-sellers collection, Gifts & Sets -> the sets collection), ideally via a bound Fluid navigation menu rather than hardcoded hrefs.
STEP_OUTPUT includes the link-audit table (label -> target -> HTTP status -> resolved template).

steps.name: Product price QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — PRICES ONLY. Visit EVERY product's PDP (enumerate via GET /api/company/v1/products) and confirm the displayed RETAIL price and, where a subscription plan exists, the SUBSCRIPTION price render on the page and MATCH the API variant data for the store's default country (variant_countries.price / subscription_price). Flag any PDP where the price is missing, $0, or differs from the API. If the store serves MULTIPLE countries, switch the storefront country (or request with the country's locale) for at least a couple of products and confirm the price + currency update correctly to that country's variant_country pricing. Do NOT check anything else (links, cart, layout are other steps). STEP_OUTPUT: a table of product -> displayed retail / subscription price -> API expected -> match?, plus any mismatches and the country-switch check result.
acceptance: Every PDP shows a non-zero retail price that matches the API variant price for the default country.
Subscription price is shown on products that have a subscription plan, and matches the API.
For multi-country stores, at least one country switch is verified to change the displayed price + currency correctly (or the report states the store is single-country).
STEP_OUTPUT lists every product's price check and names any mismatch.

steps.name: Add to cart QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — ADD TO CART ONLY. Visit EVERY PDP and confirm the add-to-cart button is correctly wired through FairShare: `data-fluid-add-to-cart="<variantId>"` is present and the id is a REAL active variant of that product; on multi-variant products it is VARIANT-AWARE (selecting a scent/size updates the button's variant id + price); `data-fluid-quantity` and `data-fluid-open-cart-after-add` are sane. Confirm the cart drawer/FairShare SDK is present (the `fluid-cdn-script` is injected). Flag any PDP with a missing, hardcoded, placeholder, or stale variant id, or a non-variant-aware selector. Do NOT check prices/links/layout. STEP_OUTPUT: a table of PDP -> data-fluid-add-to-cart value -> real active variant? -> variant-aware?, plus any failures.
acceptance: Every PDP has a data-fluid-add-to-cart bound to a real, active variant id for that product.
Multi-variant products update the add-to-cart variant id (and price) when a variant is selected.
No PDP has a missing, placeholder, or stale variant id.
STEP_OUTPUT lists every PDP's add-to-cart wiring and names any failure.

steps.name: Mobile responsive QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — MOBILE ONLY. Use the fresh-machine Mist preview capabilities, not a local/global Playwright assumption. Call start_preview if needed, confirm local URL with preview_state, then for one of EACH route type — home, collection, category (if any), product PDP, content page, cart — call screenshot_preview with `{mode:"full",path:"<route>",width:390,height:844}`. Require HTTP 200 and use the reported document width to prove no horizontal overflow. Inspect images/text/tap-target geometry in the screenshots. On the home route, inspect the real mobile-menu button selector, call interact_preview to open it, take a fresh 390x844 screenshot, then close it and recapture; aria-expanded/state and visible menu content must change. Read preview console + local server logs after the route matrix. Flag any overflow, overlap/cutoff, broken mobile nav, unreadable type, or runtime failure. Do NOT check prices/cart wiring/link targets. STEP_OUTPUT: route -> status -> viewport/document width -> screenshot paths -> issues, plus mobile-menu interaction evidence and log status.
acceptance: Every sampled route has current screenshot_preview evidence at an exact 390x844 viewport, HTTP 200, and reported document width <= 390px.
The header navigation has a working mobile state proven by interact_preview plus fresh before/open/closed screenshots and an aria-expanded or equivalent visible state change.
Primary CTAs/tap targets are adequately sized and images scale within the viewport.
Preview console and local server logs are clean after the matrix, and STEP_OUTPUT includes each route's screenshot path, viewport/document width, status, and any flagged issue.

steps.name: Product active-status QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — PRODUCT STATUS ONLY, and run this BEFORE the price/add-to-cart QA (they depend on it). The Fluid Products API can create products as `status: "draft"` when the create payload omits `status: "active"` — the switch is `PATCH /api/company/v1/products/{id}` with `{product:{status:"active"}}`. A draft product 404s its PDP and is hidden from its membership collections, which silently breaks the storefront and every downstream QA. Enumerate ALL products (GET /api/company/v1/products) and confirm each has `status == "active"` (not draft/scheduled/archived). For any product still draft, PATCH it to active. Then confirm each product's PDP renders 200 and the product appears in at least one collection it belongs to. Do NOT check price/cart/layout (other steps). STEP_OUTPUT: count of products by status, list of any drafts you activated, and PDP + collection-membership render confirmation for a sample.
acceptance: Zero products remain in draft/scheduled — every imported product is status == active.
Every product's PDP renders 200 (not 404 from a draft).
No collection is left with only draft members.
STEP_OUTPUT reports the status counts and any drafts activated.

steps.name: Storefront route health QA (browser-only)
steps.prompt:
Focused QA — ROUTE HEALTH. Assert the home index AND one of EACH resource type — collection, category (if any), product PDP, content page, cart — returns HTTP 200 with a non-trivial rendered body.

URL shape is part of the test. Fluid detail routes require `/{credit}/{resource}/{slug}`, with `home` as unattributed credit: `/home/products/<slug>`, `/home/collections/<slug>`, `/home/pages/<slug>`, `/home/posts/<slug>`. Index routes are credit-optional. Never accept a bare Shopify-style detail URL; a cached 200 there is not routing proof.

PRECHECK 1: GET `/api/application_themes/active`; compare its id to the built theme id. If different/draft, activate the built theme before continuing or report a blocker.

PRECHECK 2: group active theme templates by themeable_type and require a `default:true` template for layouts, locales, config, home_page, navbar, footer, product, collection, category, page, post, cart_page, shop_page. Fix missing defaults; do not label blank 204 routes as platform bugs.

METHODOLOGY: use Mist's managed browser. For each PUBLIC storefront URL, call crawl with `formats:["html","screenshot"]`, `only_main_content:false`, and exact viewport screenshot options. Record requested URL, final URL, metadata HTTP status, title, screenshot, and non-trivial resource-specific body. A redirect to home, generic home body, blank/loading screenshot, 204, 404, or 500 fails. For the matching LOCAL route, call screenshot_preview with path + exact viewport and record its navigation status. Read preview console/local logs. This requires no local Playwright install. If an older Mist build cannot report crawl final URL/status or exact screenshots, report tooling needs-review rather than inventing a browser pass.

STEP_OUTPUT: route type -> public requested/final URL -> public status/rendered -> local URL/status -> evidence paths; plus PRECHECK 1 active/built theme ids and PRECHECK 2 default-template table.
acceptance: PRECHECK 1 ran: the theme returned by GET /api/application_themes/active is the theme this run built (or the drift is reported as a blocker).

PRECHECK 2 ran: every required themeable_type (layouts, locales, config, home_page, navbar, footer, product, collection, category, page, post, cart_page, shop_page) has a default:true template, or the missing ones are listed and fixed.

Every sampled route type (home, collection, category, PDP, content page, cart) is asserted on the credit-prefixed public URL where required and has managed-browser evidence: requested URL == intended final route, HTTP 200, non-trivial resource-specific HTML, and a non-blank current screenshot; the matching local preview route also reports a healthy navigation status.
No route is declared healthy on the strength of a bare Shopify-style URL (`/products/<slug>`, `/collections/<slug>`) — those are cache-dependent and not a supported Fluid path.
STEP_OUTPUT reports the per-route-type browser status plus both precheck tables.

steps.name: SEO metadata QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — SEO METADATA ONLY (browser-based). For each route type (home, a collection, a product PDP, a content page), load it in a real browser and assert the <head> + document are SEO-ready: a non-empty, resource-SPECIFIC <title> (NOT empty and NOT a generic storefront default like 'Live Free.'), a meaningful <meta name=description> (not the generic default), a <link rel=canonical>, and exactly ONE <h1> with real resource content. Product and collection pages should also emit the relevant JSON-LD (Product / ItemList / BreadcrumbList). Fix what the THEME controls (title/description/canonical/h1/JSON-LD in the layout + templates, driven by the resource drop — e.g. `{{ page_title }}`, product/collection fields). FLAG what only store-level SEO settings can fix (site-wide default title/description, robots) for the human. STEP_OUTPUT: a per-route-type table -> title / description / canonical / h1 / JSON-LD present? -> pass/flag.
acceptance: Every route type has a non-empty, resource-specific <title> (not a generic default) and a meaningful meta description.
Every route type has a <link rel=canonical> and exactly one <h1> with real content.
Product and collection pages emit the relevant JSON-LD.
Theme-controllable gaps are fixed; store-level SEO-setting gaps are flagged for the human. STEP_OUTPUT lists the per-route SEO check.
Each PDP <title> contains the product name; if Fluid's layout scope makes product unavailable so the title falls to the brand default, flag it for the human rather than leaving it silently generic.

steps.name: Page route content QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — CONTENT PAGE ROUTES ONLY (browser-based). For every content/info page the onboarding authored (About, Contact, Shipping, Privacy, Terms, FAQ, Store locator, etc.), load /home/pages/<slug> in a real browser and assert the AUTHORED BODY renders — not just the nav + footer chrome. A page whose main region is empty means a page RECORD was never created (a template alone does not route content); a `/home/pages/<slug>` that 404s outright means the slug does not exist; and a page route that 204s for EVERY slug means the active theme has no `default: true` template for themeable_type `page`. CREATE the missing record via POST /api/company/pages (note: /api/company/v1/pages and /api/pages both 404 — use /api/company/pages), then re-check; html_code compiles async so re-GET/re-PATCH if the body returns empty, and use a FRESH slug (deleting a page tombstones its slug). Confirm every footer/nav link that points at a /pages/ route lands on a page with real body copy. STEP_OUTPUT: a table of page slug -> record exists? -> body renders? -> linked-from resolves? -> pass/fixed/flag.
acceptance: Every authored content page renders its real body copy in a browser, not just nav + footer.
Missing page records are created via POST /api/company/pages (fresh slug) and re-verified.
Every footer/nav link to a /pages/ route resolves to a page with real content.
STEP_OUTPUT lists per-page record-exists / body-renders / linked-from status.

steps.name: Font substitution QA
steps.prompt: Focused QA — FONT LICENSING & SUBSTITUTION ONLY. Determine the source brand's primary display + body typefaces. If a source font is proprietary (not OFL/Google-hosted/freely licensable) and was substituted with a free alternative, assert the substitution is done honestly and completely: (1) the closest free family is used consistently across the theme (no lingering references to the proprietary family name), (2) a license disclaimer naming the original font and the free substitute is embedded in the theme (e.g. a comment in layouts/theme.liquid), and (3) a sane font-stack fallback is present so text never renders in an unstyled default. If the brand's own licensed font files ARE importable (this is their store), import the real @font-face and keep the disclaimer noting the licensing assumption. STEP_OUTPUT: source font(s) -> proprietary? -> substitute used -> disclaimer present? -> fallback present? -> pass/flag.
acceptance: Source typefaces identified; any proprietary font that was substituted is called out.
Substitute family is applied consistently with no leftover proprietary-family references.
A license disclaimer (original + substitute) is embedded in the theme and a fallback stack is present.
STEP_OUTPUT lists per-font substitution + disclaimer + fallback status.

steps.name: Launch-readiness review
steps.prompt:
Produce a live-verified launch-readiness report. This is NOT a summary of what earlier steps said — every claim here must be backed by a check YOU performed this turn.

1. **Storefront live check** — from the gather-context step's context, find the company's public storefront URL (from /api/settings/companies/{id}). crawl(<url>, formats: ['screenshot']) and confirm it returns without error. If that crawl returns a SCRAPE_TIMEOUT, retry ONCE with a plain/markdown crawl (crawl(<url>) with no screenshot format — it succeeds when the screenshot renderer times out) and treat a clean plain crawl as the storefront being live BEFORE you record a storefront miss. Attach the screenshot's URL (or, on the fallback, the plain-crawl result) to the report.
2. **Theme sanity** — screenshot_preview once to confirm the theme's dev preview still renders. Read the iterative-theme-refine step's STEP_OUTPUT for any remaining majors/minors and surface them.
3. **Products** — GET /api/company/v1/products and count via meta.pagination.total_count. Spot-check 3 for non-empty title + price + at least one image. Flag any product whose title matches 'Sample Product' — that's the manual stub and it must not ship.
4. **Onboarding info** — GET /api/companies/{id}/onboarding_info (the legacy /api/v1/onboardings endpoints are removed — do not call them) and record what business/country info is on file vs still missing. Compare to what populate-getting-started reported; flag drift. CLASSIFY missing fields, do not blanket-blocker them: a field populate-getting-started listed as `deferred` with a human-input reason (KYC/payments/legal-entity — these ALWAYS need a human) is an EXPECTED gap, so surface it as a `medium`/human-action item, NOT a launch blocker. An empty `onboarding_info: {}` is therefore not automatically unlaunchable — only treat a missing field as a `high`/`blocker` when it should have been filled this run but is absent because a scrape or earlier step FAILED (not merely deferred). Reserve `blocker` for fields that truly block going live.
5. **Brand + business info** — GET /api/settings/brand_guidelines and confirm the brand color tokens from gather-context landed. If a token is still default/empty, flag it.
6. **Degraded steps** — if any earlier step finished in a degraded/needs-review state (its findings appear in your context), fold its unresolved findings into the checklist below with appropriate severity.
7. **Prioritized checklist** — assemble a `Before you launch:` list. Each entry has:
   - severity: `blocker` (unlaunchable), `high` (embarrassing at launch), `medium` (fix week 1), `low` (nice-to-have)
   - what: one line
   - why: which check this turn produced it
   - suggested action

Rank by severity. If there are zero blockers and ≤ 2 highs, say so plainly — the report is not required to invent problems.
acceptance: The report cites live checks performed THIS turn: at least one GET /api/company/v1/products, at least one GET /api/companies/{id}/onboarding_info (never the removed /api/v1/onboardings), and either a crawl-screenshot of the public storefront or an explicit 'storefront URL not yet published' note.
The 'Before you launch' checklist exists and every entry has severity + what + why + suggested action.
Any remaining majors from iterative-theme-refine's STEP_OUTPUT (and any degraded/needs-review step findings present in context) appear in the checklist with severity assigned.
The manual-stub product 'Sample Product' is either flagged as a blocker (Case C ran) or explicitly noted as absent (Case A/B ran).

Missing onboarding_info fields are classified, not blanket-blockered: KYC/payments/legal fields populate-getting-started deferred to a human are surfaced as human-action items (not launch blockers), while fields absent due to a scrape/step failure are flagged with real severity. An empty onboarding_info is not, by itself, treated as unlaunchable.
